body:
P2-25 DESIGN for P2-12 (plan PR #75): what the plan can rely on from P2-25 and what it must not. Information, not a command.

(1) Your Order line is right: slices 1 to 4 and 7 do not need P2-25, slices 5 (the typo rule N-23b and its glyph table), 6 and 8 need it (the rule tables and the phone offline index, B-84). (2) The typo form: P2-25 gives fold() as the character stage that KEEPS punctuation, so the N-23b glyph look-alike rule ($ @ ! 0 1 3 4 5 7) runs on fold(), not on the word list; words() is the second stage; one fixture, app/test/fixtures/text/fold-cases.json, read by both suites (your typo-rule.json can sit beside it and follows the same convention: both workflows list the folder). (3) The Dart fold: app/lib/domain/text_fold.dart plus a table generated from Python (tools/gen_text_fold_table.py, checked in CI); your slice 8 deletes the phone NAME MATCHING (matchKey, matchesQueryWords against the catalogue, B-46) and keeps the Dart fold: the offline index of the person's own downloads needs it. (4) B-84 stays yours (and P1-16): the FTS tokenizer needs categories 'L* N* Co M*', one token per Han, Kana or Thai character, harakat stripped on both sides, and a rebuild in a migration; P2-25 supplies the fold and the rows (RUN again: SQLite 3.50.4, unicode61 remove_diacritics 2 splits Hindi tum into two letters and Arabic with harakat into four, finds 12 and the Arabic-Indic 12 as two tokens, and does not find a Japanese name by its first three characters). (5) Identity (your D4, keyed by the music server artist id) is not touched. (6) The catalogue._FOLD copy of the phone table is replaced by the shared fold in P2-25 slice 2; its edition-suffix rule stays. (7) A new file the plan should know: P2-25 slice 3 takes the next migration number at cut time; main has 0015 and PR #94 holds 0016.
